questions.text: दो आवेश, जिनमें प्रत्येक –q है, किसी समबाहु त्रिभुज ABC के दो शीर्षों A तथा B पर स्थित हैं। यदि AB का मध्यबिन्दु M है तो C पर नेट विद्युत क्षेत्र निम्नलिखित में से किसके अनुदिश होगा?
questions.text_english: Two charges –q each are placed at the vertices A and B of an equilateral triangle ABC. If M is the mid-point of AB, the net electric field at C will point along
questions.solution: The two equal negative charges –q at A and B create electric fields at C that point from C towards A and from C towards B respectively. By symmetry, the components perpendicular to the line CM cancel, while the components along CM add up. The resultant electric field therefore points from C towards M, i.e., along CM. Options A, B, and C represent incorrect directions because the symmetry of the configuration forces the net field to lie along the axis of symmetry CM.
questions.topic: Electric field due to point charges

questions.text: किसी छात्रा के पास तीन प्रतिरोधक हैं जिनमें प्रत्येक का प्रतिरोध R है। यदि वह 2/3 R प्रतिरोध प्राप्त करना चाहती है तो उसे इन प्रतिरोधकों को किस प्रकार संयोजित करना चाहिए?
questions.text_english: A student has three resistors, each of resistance R. To obtain a resistance of 2/3 R, she should connect

options.A: सभी तीनों प्रतिरोधकों को श्रेणी में
options.B: सभी तीनों प्रतिरोधकों को पार्श्व में
options.C: दो प्रतिरोधकों के श्रेणी संयोजन को तीसरे प्रतिरोधक से पार्श्व में
options.D: दो प्रतिरोधकों के पार्श्व संयोजन को तीसरे प्रतिरोधक से श्रेणी में

options_english.A: all the three resistors in series.
options_english.B: all the three resistors in parallel.
options_english.C: two resistors in series and then this combination in parallel with the third resistor.
options_english.D: two resistors in parallel and then this combination in series with the third resistor.

questions.solution: Two resistors in parallel give R/2. Connecting this in series with the third resistor gives R/2 + R = 3R/2. That is option C gives 3R/2, not 2R/3. Let us re-examine: Two resistors in parallel = R/2. Series with third = R/2 + R = 3R/2. Two in series = 2R, parallel with third = 2R×R/(2R+R) = 2R/3. So option D is correct: two resistors in series (giving 2R) connected in parallel with the third resistor (R) gives an equivalent resistance of 2R×R/(2R+R) = 2R²/3R = 2R/3, which is the required resistance.
questions.topic: Combination of resistors

questions.text: किसी धारावाही चालक, जिससे x-दिशा में 1A धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है, का 1 cm लम्बा सीधा खण्ड कार्तीय निर्देशांक प्रणाली के मूलबिन्दु पर सममिततः रखा है। इस खण्ड के कारण बिन्दु (1m, 1m, 0) पर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र है
questions.text_english: A 1 cm straight segment of a conductor carrying 1 A current in x direction lies symmetrically at origin of Cartesian coordinate system. The magnetic field due to this segment at point (1m, 1m, 0) is
questions.solution: Using Biot-Savart law: dB = (μ₀/4π) × (I dl × r̂)/r². The current element is I dl = 1 × 0.01 î A·m. The position vector from origin to point (1,1,0) is r = î + ĵ, |r| = √2 m. The cross product dl × r̂ = î × (î+ĵ)/√2 = ĵ/√2 × ... gives a component in k̂ direction. Computing: dB = (10⁻⁷) × (0.01 × sin45°)/(√2)² k̂ = (10⁻⁷ × 0.01 × 1/√2)/2 k̂ = (5.0/√2) × 10⁻¹⁰ k̂ T. The positive k̂ direction confirms option C. Options A and B have incorrect magnitude, and D has a wrong sign.
questions.topic: Biot-Savart Law

questions.text: द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण 'M' के किसी लघु चुम्बकीय द्विध्रुव के कारण उसके अक्ष के अनुदिश उसके केन्द्र से दूरी 'r' पर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र होगा –
questions.text_english: The magnetic field due to a small magnetic dipole of dipole moment 'M' at a distance 'r' from the centre along the axis of the dipole is given by
questions.solution: The standard formula for the magnetic field on the axial line (end-on position) of a magnetic dipole is B = (μ₀/4π) × (2M/r³). This is derived from the expression for the magnetic field due to a bar magnet along its axis. Options B and C give wrong numerical factors, and option D has an incorrect power of r (r² instead of r³). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.topic: Magnetic dipole field on axial line

questions.text: आरेख में लकड़ी के किसी खोखले पाइप से कुण्डली X लिपटी है। किसी स्थायी चुम्बक को दायीं ओर से नियत वेग v से इस पाइप के भीतर धकेला गया है तथा यह पाइप के बायीं ओर से बाहर आता है। चुम्बक के प्रवेश करते और बाहर निकलते समय तार YZ में धारा की दिशा होगी
questions.text_english: In the figure X is a coil wound over a hollow wooden pipe. A permanent magnet is pushed at a constant speed v from the right into the pipe and it comes out at the left end of the pipe. During the entry and the exit of the magnet, the current in the wire YZ will be from

options.A: Y से Z की ओर और फिर Y से Z की ओर
options.B: Z से Y की ओर और फिर Y से Z की ओर
options.C: Y से Z की ओर और फिर Z से Y की ओर
options.D: Z से Y की ओर और फिर Z से Y की ओर

options_english.A: Y to Z and then Y to Z
options_english.B: Z to Y and then Y to Z
options_english.C: Y to Z and then Z to Y
options_english.D: Z to Y and then Z to Y

questions.solution: As the magnet enters from the right with its north pole leading, the flux through the coil increases. By Lenz's law, the induced current opposes this increase, creating a magnetic field opposing the north pole — the induced current flows from Y to Z in wire YZ. As the magnet exits from the left side (north pole leading left), the flux through the coil decreases. By Lenz's law, the induced current now tries to maintain the flux, reversing its direction — current flows from Z to Y in wire YZ. Hence the answer is option C.
questions.topic: Lenz's Law and induced current direction

questions.text: किसी प्रेरक से प्रवाहित प्रत्यावर्ती धारा I का समय t के साथ एक चक्र के प्रवाह में आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार विचरण का प्रेक्षण किया गया। नीचे दिया गया कौन सा आरेख तरंग रूप वोल्टता V का समय t के साथ सही विचरण निरूपित करता है?
questions.text_english: The alternating current I in an inductor is observed to vary with time t as shown in the graph for a cycle. Which one of the following graphs is the correct representation of wave form of voltage V with time t?

options.A: Triangular wave in phase with current
options.B: Wave with positive peak before T/2 and negative trough after T/2

options_english.A: Triangular wave in phase with current
options_english.B: Wave with positive peak before T/2 and negative trough after T/2

questions.solution: For an inductor, the voltage is V = L × dI/dt. Since the current waveform is triangular (linearly increasing from 0 to T/2, then linearly decreasing from T/2 to T), the derivative dI/dt is constant and positive during the first half and constant and negative during the second half. Therefore, the voltage waveform is a square wave — constant positive voltage for the first half cycle and constant negative voltage for the second half cycle. This corresponds to option C.
questions.topic: Voltage across an inductor

questions.text: कोई ट्रान्सफॉर्मर 200 V ac स्रोत से संयोजित है। यह ट्रान्सफॉर्मर किसी युक्ति को 3000 V की आपूर्ति करता है। यदि प्राथमिक कुण्डली में फेरों की संख्या 450 है, तो इसकी द्वितीयक कुण्डली में फेरों की संख्या होगी –
questions.text_english: A transformer is connected to a 200 V ac source. The transformer supplies 3000 V to a device. If the number of turns in the primary coil is 450, then the number of turns in its secondary coil is –
questions.solution: Using the transformer equation: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. Here Vs = 3000 V, Vp = 200 V, Np = 450. Therefore Ns = Np × (Vs/Vp) = 450 × (3000/200) = 450 × 15 = 6750. The secondary coil must have 6750 turns. Options A, B, and C arise from incorrect calculations or ratios.
questions.topic: Transformer turns ratio

questions.text: नीचे दिया गया कौन सा एक कथन सही है? स्थिर आवेशों के कारण उत्पन्न विद्युत क्षेत्र
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is correct? Electric field due to static charges is

options.A: संरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश नहीं बनाती हैं।
options.B: संरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश बनाती हैं।
options.C: असंरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश नहीं बनाती हैं।
options.D: असंरक्षी होता है तथा क्षेत्र रेखाएँ बन्द पाश बनाती हैं।

options_english.A: conservative and field lines do not form closed loops.
options_english.B: conservative and field lines form closed loops.
options_english.C: non-conservative and field lines do not form closed loops.
options_english.D: non-conservative and field lines form closed loops.

questions.solution: The electric field due to static charges is always conservative in nature, meaning the work done in moving a charge along any closed path is zero. Electrostatic field lines originate on positive charges and terminate on negative charges — they never form closed loops. This is a fundamental property of electrostatic (irrotational) fields. Option B is wrong because static field lines do not form closed loops; options C and D are wrong because the field is conservative, not non-conservative.
questions.topic: Properties of electric field lines

questions.text: कोई टब 30.0 cm ऊँचाई तक किसी पारदर्शी द्रव से भरा है। इस टब की तली पर रखे किसी सिक्के की आभासी गहराई 16.0 cm पायी जाती है। इस द्रव में प्रकाश की चाल होगी
questions.text_english: A tub is filled with a transparent liquid to a height of 30.0 cm. The apparent depth of a coin lying at the bottom of the tub is found to be 16.0 cm. The speed of light in the liquid will be
questions.solution: The refractive index n = real depth / apparent depth = 30.0 / 16.0 = 1.875. The speed of light in the medium is v = c/n = (3 × 10⁸)/1.875 = 1.6 × 10⁸ m/s. Wait — recalculating: n = 30/16 = 1.875, v = 3×10⁸/1.875 = 1.6×10⁸. So the answer should be option A. However, if the intended calculation uses n = 30/16 ≈ 1.5, that gives v = 2.0×10⁸. With n = 30/16 = 15/8, v = 3×10⁸ × 8/15 = 1.6×10⁸ m/s. The correct answer is option A: 1.6 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, since n = real depth/apparent depth = 30/16 = 1.875, giving v = c/n = 3×10⁸/1.875 = 1.6×10⁸ m/s.
questions.topic: Refraction and apparent depth

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु की परमाणु स्पेक्ट्रमी उत्सर्जन रेखाएँ किसी जिंक पृष्ठ पर आपतन कर रही हैं। वह रेखाएँ जो इस पृष्ठ से फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों का उत्सर्जन करा सकती हैं, निम्नलिखित में से किसकी सदस्य हैं?
questions.text_english: Atomic spectral emission lines of hydrogen atom are incident on a zinc surface. The lines which can emit photoelectrons from the surface are members of

options.D: न तो बामर, न ही पाशन और न ही लाइमेन श्रेणी

options_english.D: Neither Balmer, nor Paschen nor Lyman series

questions.solution: The work function of zinc is approximately 4.3 eV. To emit photoelectrons, the photon energy must exceed this work function. The Lyman series lies in the ultraviolet region with photon energies ranging from about 10.2 eV to 13.6 eV, all of which are greater than 4.3 eV. The Balmer series lies in the visible/near-UV range with energies from about 1.9 eV to 3.4 eV, which are below the work function. The Paschen series lies in the infrared region with even lower photon energies. Therefore, only the Lyman series photons can eject photoelectrons from zinc, making option C correct.
questions.topic: Hydrogen spectrum and photoelectric effect

questions.text: किसी हाइड्रोजन परमाणु में किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन की निम्नतम अवस्था में ऊर्जा –13.6 eV है। क्वान्टम संख्या n के तद्नुरूप किसी कक्षा में इसकी ऊर्जा –0.544 eV है। n का मान है
questions.text_english: The energy of an electron in a hydrogen atom in ground state is –13.6 eV. Its energy in an orbit corresponding to quantum number n is –0.544 eV. The value of n is
questions.solution: The energy of an electron in the nth orbit of hydrogen is Eₙ = –13.6/n² eV. Given Eₙ = –0.544 eV, we have –13.6/n² = –0.544, which gives n² = 13.6/0.544 = 25, so n = 5. Therefore option D is correct. Checking: E₅ = –13.6/25 = –0.544 eV, which matches the given value perfectly.
questions.topic: Bohr model energy levels

questions.text: जब किसी p-n संधि डायोड के p और n सिरों के बीच मापित प्रतिरोध उच्च होता है, तब यह निम्नलिखित में से किसकी भाँति कार्य कर सकता है?
questions.text_english: When the resistance measured between p and n ends of a p-n junction diode is high, it can act as a/an –
questions.solution: When the resistance between the p and n terminals of a p-n junction diode is very high (i.e., under reverse bias), very little current flows. In this state, the depletion region acts as a dielectric layer between the p-type and n-type semiconductor regions, which function like two conducting plates. This configuration is exactly that of a capacitor (parallel plate capacitor). Hence the diode under high resistance (reverse bias) condition acts as a capacitor. Options A, B, and D are incorrect because the diode does not behave as a resistor, inductor, or switch in this state.
questions.topic: p-n junction diode characteristics

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : किसी अर्धचालक डायोड में ह्रासी स्तर की मोटाई अचर नहीं होती है।
कारण (R) : अर्धचालक युक्तियों में ह्रासी स्तर की मोटाई बहुत से कारकों, जैसे अर्धचालक के बायसन पर निर्भर करती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : In a semiconductor diode the thickness of depletion layer is not fixed.
Reason (R) : Thickness of depletion layer in a semiconductor device depends upon many factors such as biasing of the semiconductor.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) के लिए सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below for Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The Assertion is true: the thickness of the depletion layer in a semiconductor diode is not fixed — it changes with the applied bias. The Reason is also true: the depletion layer width depends on factors like the type of bias (forward or reverse), the magnitude of the applied voltage, and doping concentrations. Furthermore, the Reason correctly explains the Assertion — the depletion layer is not of fixed thickness precisely because it depends on biasing and other factors. Hence option A is the correct answer.
questions.topic: Depletion layer in p-n junction

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर मॉडल में nवीं कक्षा के इलेक्ट्रॉन का कोणीय संवेग उसकी कक्षा की त्रिज्या rₙ के वर्गमूल के अनुपाती होता है।
कारण (R) : बोर मॉडल के अनुसार कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन केवल अपनी निकटतम कक्षाओं तक कूदान कर सकता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : In Bohr model of hydrogen atom, the angular momentum of an electron in nth orbit is proportional to the square root of its orbit radius rₙ.
Reason (R) : According to Bohr model, electron can jump to its nearest orbits only.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) के लिए सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer for Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The Assertion is true: in Bohr's model, the angular momentum L = nh/2π ∝ n, and the orbit radius rₙ ∝ n², so n ∝ √rₙ, which means L ∝ √rₙ. The Assertion is therefore correct. The Reason, however, is false: according to Bohr's model, an electron can jump between any two allowed orbits, not just the nearest ones. There is no restriction to adjacent orbits in Bohr's postulates. Hence option C is correct — Assertion is true but Reason is false.
questions.topic: Bohr model of hydrogen atom

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : अवरक्त तरंगों और रेडियो तरंगों में से रेडियो तरंगें विस्तृत विवर्तन प्रभाव दर्शा सकती हैं।
कारण (R) : अवरक्त तरंगों की तुलना में रेडियो तरंगों की आवृत्ति अधिक होती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Out of Infrared and radio waves, the radio waves show more diffraction effect.
Reason (R) : Radio waves have greater frequency than infrared waves.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) के लिए सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer for Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The Assertion is true: radio waves show more diffraction than infrared waves because diffraction is prominent when the wavelength is comparable to or larger than the obstacle/aperture size. Radio waves have much longer wavelengths than infrared waves, so they diffract more easily around buildings and hills. The Reason, however, is false: radio waves actually have lower frequency (and hence longer wavelength) than infrared waves, not greater frequency. The correct explanation for more diffraction is greater wavelength, not greater frequency. Hence option C is correct.
questions.topic: Diffraction of electromagnetic waves

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : किसी आदर्श अपचायी ट्रान्सफॉर्मर में विद्युत ऊर्जा का क्षय नहीं होता है।
कारण (R) : किसी अपचायी ट्रान्सफॉर्मर में वोल्टता घटती है, परन्तु धारा बढ़ती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : In an ideal step-down transformer, the electrical energy is not lost.
Reason (R) : In a step-down transformer, voltage decreases but the current increases.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) के लिए सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer for Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: If Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: If both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: The Assertion is true: in an ideal transformer, there are no energy losses — the output power equals the input power (VpIp = VsIs). The Reason is also true: in a step-down transformer, the secondary voltage is less than the primary voltage, but to conserve power, the secondary current is proportionally greater. However, the Reason does not correctly explain the Assertion. The Assertion is about no energy loss (ideal condition), while the Reason describes voltage-current behavior in a step-down transformer, which is a consequence of energy conservation, not the explanation for no energy loss. Hence option B is correct.
questions.topic: Transformer — ideal operation

questions.text:
(a) समान पदार्थ और समान त्रिज्या के दो तार, जिनकी लम्बाइयों का अनुपात 2 : 3 है, किसी बैटरी से जो 15 A धारा की आपूर्ति करती है, पार्श्व में संयोजित हैं। इन तारों से प्रवाहित धारा ज्ञात कीजिए।
अथवा
(b) चित्र में दर्शाए अनुसार एक परिपथ में V, V तथा 2V वि.वा.ब. के तीन आदर्श सेलों को R प्रतिरोधकता के एक प्रतिरोधक, C धारिता के एक संधारित्र तथा 2R प्रतिरोधकता के एक अन्य प्रतिरोधक से जोड़ा गया है। स्थायी अवस्था में ज्ञात कीजिए (i) P तथा Q के मध्य विभवांतर तथा (ii) संधारित्र C के सिरों पर विभवांतर।
questions.text_english:
(a) Two wires of the same material and the same radius have their lengths in the ratio 2 : 3. They are connected in parallel to a battery which supplies a current of 15 A. Find the current through the wires.
OR
(b) In the circuit three ideal cells of e.m.f. V, V and 2V are connected to a resistor of resistance R, a capacitor of capacitance C and another resistor of resistance 2R as shown in figure. In the steady state find (i) the potential difference between P and Q and (ii) potential difference across capacitor C.

key_points: Resistance is proportional to length for same material and radius: R ∝ L
R₁/R₂ = L₁/L₂ = 2/3
In parallel, current divides inversely as resistance
I₁/I₂ = R₂/R₁ = 3/2, and I₁ + I₂ = 15 A
Solving: I₁ = 6 A, I₂ = 9 A

questions.solution:
Part (a): Since both wires are of the same material and radius, their resistance is proportional to length. So R₁ : R₂ = 2 : 3. In parallel combination, the currents distribute inversely proportional to resistance: I₁ : I₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 3 : 2. Since I₁ + I₂ = 15 A, we get 3x + 2x = 15, so x = 3. Therefore, I₁ = 9 A (through shorter wire) and I₂ = 6 A (through longer wire).

Part (b): In steady state, no current flows through the capacitor branch. The net EMF of the circuit is V + 2V – V = 2V (applying Kirchhoff's voltage law around the loop). Total resistance = R + 2R = 3R. Current I = 2V/3R. Potential difference between P and Q: VPQ = 2V (considering the cell arrangement). Voltage across capacitor C = potential difference across its branch = V (the EMF of the middle cell, since no current flows through capacitor branch in steady state).
questions.topic: Resistors in parallel; steady-state capacitor circuits

questions.text: किसी द्विझिरी प्रयोग में पर्दे के किसी बिन्दु पर 6वीं काली फ्रिंज बनती है। व्यतिकरण करती दो तरंगों में से एक तरंग की कला में 2π (n – 1) t/λ की वृद्धि करने के लिए उसके पथ में मोटाई t तथा अपवर्तनांक n की कोई पारदर्शी शीट रख दी जाती है। व्यतिकरण पैटर्न स्थानान्तरित हो जाता है और अब उसी स्थान पर 8वीं चमकीली फ्रिंज बन जाती है। n और λ के पदों में मोटाई t के लिए संबंध ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: In a double-slit experiment, 6th dark fringe is observed at a certain point of the screen. A transparent sheet of thickness t and refractive index n is now introduced in the path of one of the two interfering waves to increase its phase by 2π (n – 1) t/λ. The pattern is shifted and 8th bright fringe is observed at the same point. Find the relation for thickness t in terms of n and λ.

key_points: Path difference for 6th dark fringe: Δ = (2×6 – 1)λ/2 = 11λ/2
After sheet, the same point shows 8th bright fringe: new path difference = 8λ
The sheet adds extra path: (n-1)t
New path difference = old path difference + (n-1)t

questions.solution: The path difference for the 6th dark fringe at the given point is Δ₁ = (2×6 – 1)λ/2 = 11λ/2. After introducing the transparent sheet, the same point corresponds to the 8th bright fringe, so the new path difference is Δ₂ = 8λ. The sheet of thickness t and refractive index n introduces an extra optical path of (n – 1)t. Therefore: Δ₂ = Δ₁ + (n – 1)t, giving 8λ = 11λ/2 + (n – 1)t. Solving: (n – 1)t = 8λ – 11λ/2 = 16λ/2 – 11λ/2 = 5λ/2. Thus, t = 5λ / [2(n – 1)].
questions.topic: Young's double slit experiment — shift due to transparent sheet

questions.text: आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार दो अवतल लेंस A और B, जिनमें प्रत्येक की फोकस दूरी 8.0 cm है, एक दूसरे से 16 cm दूर पर समाक्ष व्यवस्थित किए गए हैं। लेंस A से 4.0 cm दूरी पर किसी बिम्ब P को रखा गया है। अन्तिम प्रतिबिम्ब की स्थिति और प्रकृति ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Two concave lenses A and B, each of focal length 8.0 cm are arranged coaxially 16 cm apart as shown in figure. An object P is placed at a distance of 4.0 cm from A. Find the position and nature of the final image formed.

key_points: For lens A: u = -4 cm, f = -8 cm; 1/v – 1/u = 1/f gives v = -8/3 cm
Image from A is virtual, 8/3 cm to the left of A
This image serves as object for lens B: distance from B = 16 + 8/3 = 56/3 cm, so u₂ = -56/3 cm
Final image is virtual, erect, diminished, located 5.6 cm to the left of lens B

questions.solution: For lens A (concave, f = –8 cm), object distance u = –4 cm. Using lens formula: 1/v – 1/u = 1/f → 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = –1/8 + 1/(–4) = –1/8 – 1/4 = –3/8, so v = –8/3 ≈ –2.67 cm. The first image I₁ is virtual and formed 8/3 cm to the left of lens A. The object distance for lens B: u₂ = –(16 + 8/3) = –(56/3) cm. For lens B: 1/v₂ = 1/f + 1/u₂ = –1/8 – 3/56 = –7/56 – 3/56 = –10/56 = –5/28. So v₂ = –28/5 = –5.6 cm. The final image is virtual, erect, and diminished, located 5.6 cm to the left of lens B.
questions.topic: Image formation by combination of lenses

questions.text: कार्य फलन 3.0 × 10⁻¹⁹ J के किसी धातु के पृष्ठ पर 400 nm तरंगदैर्ध्य का प्रकाश आपतन करता है। उत्सर्जित होने वाले तीव्रतम फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉन की चाल परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: A light of wavelength 400 nm is incident on metal surface whose work function is 3.0 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Calculate the speed of the fastest photoelectrons emitted.
questions.solution: Energy of the incident photon: E = hc/λ = (6.63×10⁻³⁴ × 3×10⁸)/(400×10⁻⁹) = 4.97×10⁻¹⁹ J. The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is KE_max = E – φ = 4.97×10⁻¹⁹ – 3.0×10⁻¹⁹ = 1.97×10⁻¹⁹ J. Using ½mv² = KE_max: v = √(2 × 1.97×10⁻¹⁹ / 9.1×10⁻³¹) = √(4.33×10¹¹) ≈ 6.58×10⁵ m/s. The speed of the fastest photoelectrons emitted is approximately 6.58 × 10⁵ m/s.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photoelectric effect — maximum speed of photoelectrons

questions.text: सिलिकॉन डायोड की देहली वोल्टता 0.7 V है। इस बिन्दु पर V वोल्ट की किसी बैटरी के साथ श्रेणी में डायोड और 1000 Ω के किसी प्रतिरोधक को संयोजित करके इसे प्रचालित किया गया है। उस स्थिति में V का मान ज्ञात कीजिए जब ली गयी धारा 15 mA है।
questions.text_english: The threshold voltage of a silicon diode is 0.7 V. It is operated at this point by connecting the diode in series with a battery of V volt and a resistor of 1000 Ω. Find the value of V when the current drawn is 15 mA.

key_points: V = V_diode + V_resistor
V_diode = 0.7 V (threshold voltage)
V_resistor = I × R = 15×10⁻³ × 1000 = 15 V

questions.solution: By Kirchhoff's voltage law, the supply voltage V equals the sum of voltage drop across the diode and voltage drop across the resistor. The diode drops its threshold voltage of 0.7 V during conduction. The voltage across the 1000 Ω resistor is V_R = I × R = 15 × 10⁻³ × 1000 = 15 V. Therefore, V = 0.7 + 15 = 15.7 V.
questions.topic: p-n junction diode — forward bias circuit

questions.text:
(a) वि.वा.ब. E और आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध r का कोई सेल किसी परिवर्ती प्रतिरोध R और किसी वोल्टमीटर जो R के सिरों पर विभवपात दर्शाता है, से संयोजित है। V, E, R और r के बीच संबंध प्राप्त कीजिए।
(b) किसी सेल से ली गयी धारा I को फलन के रूप में लेकर सेल की टर्मिनल वोल्टता V में विचरण को दर्शाने वाले ग्राफ की आकृति खींचिए। इस ग्राफ से सेल का वि.वा.ब. और इसका आन्तरिक प्रतिरोध कैसे निर्धारित किया जा सकता है?
questions.text_english:
(a) A cell of e.m.f. E and internal resistance r is connected with a variable external resistance R and a voltmeter showing potential drop V across R. Obtain the relationship between V, E, R and r.
(b) Draw the shape of the graph showing the variation of terminal voltage V of the cell as a function of current I drawn from it. How one can determine the e.m.f. of the cell and its internal resistance from this graph?

key_points: Current in circuit: I = E/(R+r)
Terminal voltage V = E – Ir = IR
From V = IR: I = V/R; substituting into E = I(R+r) gives E = V(R+r)/R
Therefore V = ER/(R+r)
Graph: V vs I is a straight line with negative slope; y-intercept = E (when I=0), slope = –r

questions.solution:
Part (a): The current drawn from the cell is I = E/(R + r). The terminal voltage across R is V = IR = E·R/(R + r). Rearranging: V(R + r) = ER → VR + Vr = ER → V = E – Vr/R. More directly, since V = E – Ir, and I = E/(R+r), we get the relation V = ER/(R + r).

Part (b): The terminal voltage is V = E – Ir. This is a linear equation of the form y = c – mx, so the graph of V versus I is a straight line with a negative slope. The y-intercept (when I = 0) gives the e.m.f. E of the cell. The magnitude of the slope of the line gives the internal resistance r of the cell (slope = –r). The x-intercept gives the short-circuit current E/r.
questions.topic: EMF and internal resistance of a cell

questions.text:
(a) एकसमान विद्युत क्षेत्र E के प्रदेश में XX' अक्ष के संपाती किसी धारावाही लम्बे सीधे चालक जिससे –X अक्ष की ओर धारा I प्रवाहित हो रही है, के निकट कोई ऋणावेशित कण किसी नियत वेग v⃗ = –v₀î से गतिमान है। यह कण चालक से दूरी d पर रह रहा है।
(i) विद्युत क्षेत्र और चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र की दिशाओं को दर्शाने वाला आरेख खींचिए।
(ii) आवेशित कण पर लगने वाले विभिन्न बलों का उल्लेख कीजिए।
(iii) E, d और I के पदों में v₀ का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
अथवा
(b) XX' और YY' अक्षों के अनुदिश रखे दो अनन्त लम्बाई के चालकों से I₁ और I₂ धाराएँ क्रमशः –X अक्ष और –Y अक्ष के अनुदिश प्रवाहित हो रही हैं। बिन्दु P(X, Y) पर उत्पन्न नेट चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र का परिमाण और दिशा ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) In a region of a uniform electric field E, a negatively charged particle is moving with a constant velocity v⃗ = –v₀î near a long straight conductor coinciding with XX' axis and carrying current I towards –X axis. The particle remains at a distance d from the conductor.
(i) Draw diagram showing direction of electric and magnetic fields.
(ii) What are the various forces acting on the charged particle?
(iii) Find the value of v₀ in terms of E, d and I.
OR
(b) Two infinitely long conductors kept along XX' and YY' axes are carrying current I₁ and I₂ along –X axis and –Y axis respectively. Find the magnitude and direction of the net magnetic field produced at point P(X, Y).

key_points: Magnetic field due to conductor at distance d: B = μ₀I/(2πd), direction determined by right-hand rule
Forces on negative charge: gravity (downward), electric force qE, magnetic force qv×B
For constant velocity: net force = 0 → electric force balances magnetic force
qE = qv₀B → v₀ = E/B = E × 2πd/(μ₀I) = 2πEd/(μ₀I)

questions.solution:
Part (a): The long conductor carries current along –X direction. By right-hand rule, the magnetic field at a point below the conductor (in the region where the negative charge moves) is directed along +Z direction (out of the page if the charge is below and to the right). The uniform electric field E is in the –Y direction (downward, to balance the magnetic force on the negative charge).

(i) The electric field E points downward (–ĵ direction) and the magnetic field B due to the current-carrying wire points in the +k̂ direction at the location of the particle.

(ii) The forces on the negatively charged particle are: (1) Electric force F_E = qE upward (since charge is negative and field is downward, force is upward), (2) Magnetic force F_B = q(v⃗ × B⃗) acting downward, and (3) Gravitational force (neglected in most cases).

(iii) For constant velocity, the net force is zero. The magnetic field at distance d from the wire is B = μ₀I/(2πd). Balancing electric and magnetic forces on the charge: qE = qv₀B → v₀ = E/B = E × 2πd/(μ₀I) = 2πEd/(μ₀I).
questions.topic: Magnetic force on moving charge; current-carrying conductor

questions.text:
(a) लेंज का नियम लिखिए।
(b) दिए गए आरेख में:
(i) मशीन की पहचान कीजिए।
(ii) मशीन के भागों P, Q तथा R के नाम लिखिए।
(iii) चुम्बकीय ध्रुवों की ध्रुवता दीजिए।
(iv) निर्गत वोल्टता में वृद्धि करने के दो उपाय लिखिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) State Lenz's law.
(b) In the given figure:
(i) Identify the machine.
(ii) Name the parts P and Q and R of the machine.
(iii) Give the polarities of the magnetic poles.
(iv) Write the two ways of increasing the output voltage.

key_points: Lenz's law: induced current direction opposes the cause producing it
The machine is an AC generator (alternator)
P = slip rings, Q = brushes, R = armature coil (rectangular coil)
Magnetic poles: left pole is N (north) and right pole is S (south)
Output voltage increased by: increasing speed of rotation, using stronger magnets/increasing number of turns

questions.solution:
Part (a): Lenz's law states that the direction of the induced current in a circuit is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that causes it. In other words, the induced EMF always acts to oppose the cause that produces it, which is a consequence of the law of conservation of energy.

Part (b): (i) The machine shown is an AC generator (alternator). (ii) P represents the slip rings, Q represents the carbon brushes, and R represents the armature coil (rectangular rotating coil). (iii) The left magnetic pole is the North pole (N) and the right magnetic pole is the South pole (S), as indicated by the field direction. (iv) The output voltage can be increased by (1) increasing the number of turns in the armature coil, and (2) increasing the speed of rotation of the coil (or equivalently, using a stronger magnetic field).
questions.topic: Lenz's law; AC Generator

questions.text:
(a) उत्तर दिशा में संचरण करती किसी विद्युत चुम्बकीय तरंग का विद्युत क्षेत्र E⃗ ऊपर-नीचे की दिशा में दोलन कर रहा है। इस तरंग के चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B⃗ की दिशा का वर्णन कीजिए।
(b) क्या रेडियो तरंगों तथा सूक्ष्म तरंगों की तरंगदैर्ध्य मानव नेत्रों द्वारा संसूचित करने वाली तरंगदैर्ध्यों से लम्बी अथवा छोटी होती है?
(c) मानव जीवन के लिए निम्नलिखित में से प्रत्येक का मुख्य उपयोग लिखिए:
(i) अवरक्त तरंगें (ii) गामा किरणें
questions.text_english:
(a) The electric field E⃗ of an electromagnetic wave propagating in north direction is oscillating in up and down direction. Describe the direction of magnetic field B⃗ of the wave.
(b) Are the wave length of radio waves and microwaves longer or shorter than those detectable by human eyes?
(c) Write main use of each of the following in human life:
(i) Infrared waves (ii) Gamma rays

key_points: B⃗ is perpendicular to both E⃗ and direction of propagation; if E is up-down (vertical) and propagation is north, then B is east-west (horizontal)
Radio waves and microwaves have longer wavelengths than visible light
Infrared: used in remote controls, thermal imaging, physiotherapy
Gamma rays: used in cancer treatment (radiotherapy), sterilisation of medical equipment

questions.solution:
Part (a): In an electromagnetic wave, the electric field E⃗, magnetic field B⃗, and direction of propagation are mutually perpendicular. The wave propagates northward, and E⃗ oscillates vertically (up-down). By the right-hand rule (E⃗ × B⃗ gives the propagation direction), B⃗ must oscillate in the east-west (horizontal) direction, perpendicular to both the north direction and the vertical direction.

Part (b): Radio waves and microwaves have much longer wavelengths than visible light. The human eye detects wavelengths in the range of about 400 nm to 700 nm (visible spectrum). Radio waves range from millimetres to kilometres and microwaves from 1 mm to 1 m — both are longer than the wavelengths detectable by human eyes.

Part (c): (i) Infrared waves are used in remote controls for electronic devices, in thermal imaging cameras, in physiotherapy for muscle relaxation, and in night vision equipment. (ii) Gamma rays are used in cancer treatment (radiation therapy to destroy tumour cells), in sterilising medical equipment and food, and in industrial radiography for detecting structural flaws.
questions.topic: Nature and uses of electromagnetic waves

questions.text:
(a) जब कोई समान्तर प्रकाश पुंज जल पृष्ठ में किसी कोण पर तिर्यकतः प्रवेश करता है, तो उस पुंज की मोटाई पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है?
(b) किरण आरेख की सहायता से यह दर्शाइए कि पानी में आंशिक रूप से डूबी कोई स्ट्रॉ झुकी प्रतीत होती है और इसकी व्याख्या कीजिए।
(c) आरेख की सहायता से किसी प्रकाशिक तन्तु द्वारा किसी प्रकाशिक सिगनल के संचरण की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) When a parallel beam of light enters water surface obliquely at some angle, what is the effect on the width of the beam?
(b) With the help of a ray diagram, show that a straw appears bent when it is partly dipped in water and explain it.
(c) Explain the transmission of optical signal through an optical fibre by a diagram.

key_points: When light enters water obliquely, the beam width decreases (narrows) because light bends towards the normal
A straw appears bent due to refraction: light from the submerged portion bends away from normal when emerging, making it appear at a different position
Optical fibre works on total internal reflection: light undergoes repeated TIR at the core-cladding interface

questions.solution:
Part (a): When a parallel beam of light enters water obliquely, it bends towards the normal (since water is optically denser than air). As each ray bends towards the normal upon entering the denser medium, the rays get closer to each other, and the width of the beam decreases (the beam narrows).

Part (b): When a straw is partly dipped in water, the part below the water surface appears bent or displaced. This is due to refraction of light at the water-air interface. Light rays from the submerged portion of the straw travel from water (denser) to air (rarer) and bend away from the normal. To an observer looking from above, these refracted rays appear to come from a position that is higher and shifted, making the straw appear bent at the water surface.

Part (c): An optical fibre consists of a glass core surrounded by a cladding of slightly lower refractive index. Light is launched into the fibre at an angle greater than the critical angle with respect to the core-cladding boundary. The light undergoes total internal reflection repeatedly at the interface and travels along the length of the fibre without any energy loss. This phenomenon allows optical signals (data) to be transmitted over long distances with very low attenuation.
questions.topic: Refraction of light; Total internal reflection; Optical fibre

questions.text_english:
(a) Show the variation of binding energy per nucleon with mass number. Write the significance of the binding energy curve.
(b) Two nuclei with lower binding energy per nucleon form a nuclei with more binding energy per nucleon.
(i) What type of nuclear reaction is it?
(ii) Whether the total mass of nuclei increases, decreases or remains unchanged?
(iii) Does the process require energy or produce energy?

key_points: Binding energy per nucleon peaks around mass number 56 (iron)
Light nuclei (low A) and heavy nuclei (high A) have lower BE per nucleon
Significance: explains why fusion releases energy for light nuclei and fission releases energy for heavy nuclei
Two light nuclei combining to form heavier nucleus = nuclear fusion
Total mass decreases (mass defect converted to energy via E=mc²)
Energy is produced (released) in the process

questions.solution:
Part (a): The binding energy per nucleon (BE/A) versus mass number (A) graph starts low for very light nuclei, rises steeply, reaches a maximum of about 8.7 MeV/nucleon near A = 56 (iron), and then gradually decreases for heavier nuclei. Significance: (1) Nuclei near A = 56 are the most stable. (2) For lighter nuclei (low A), fusion of two nuclei produces a more stable nucleus with higher BE/A, releasing energy. (3) For heavier nuclei (high A), fission into two lighter nuclei increases BE/A, also releasing energy. The curve thus explains both nuclear fusion and fission as energy-releasing processes.

Part (b): (i) When two nuclei of lower binding energy per nucleon combine to form a nucleus of higher binding energy per nucleon, the reaction is nuclear fusion. (ii) The total mass of the product nuclei is less than the sum of masses of the reactant nuclei. This decrease in mass (mass defect) is converted into energy according to Einstein's relation E = mc². (iii) The process produces (releases) energy, since the product is more tightly bound and the excess mass is liberated as kinetic energy of the products.
questions.topic: Binding energy per nucleon; Nuclear fusion

questions.text_english:
(a) What are majority and minority charge carriers in an extrinsic semiconductor?
(b) A p-n junction is forward biased. Describe the movement of the charge carriers which produce current in it.
(c) The graph shows the variation of current with voltage for a p-n junction diode. Estimate the dynamic resistance of diode at V = –0.6 volt.

key_points: n-type: majority = electrons, minority = holes; p-type: majority = holes, minority = electrons
In forward bias: holes in p-side move towards junction, electrons in n-side move towards junction, they recombine at junction producing current
Dynamic resistance = ΔV/ΔI; from graph at V = -0.6 V (reverse bias region), change in current is very small for small change in voltage
From graph: ΔV ≈ 0.2 V and ΔI ≈ 1 mA (reading from reverse bias region), so r_d ≈ 200 Ω (approximate)

questions.solution:
Part (a): In an n-type extrinsic semiconductor, electrons are the majority charge carriers and holes are the minority charge carriers. In a p-type extrinsic semiconductor, holes are the majority charge carriers and electrons are the minority charge carriers.

Part (b): When a p-n junction is forward biased, the positive terminal of the battery is connected to the p-side and the negative terminal to the n-side. This reduces the potential barrier at the junction. The majority charge carriers — holes in the p-region — move towards the junction and cross into the n-region, while electrons (majority carriers in n-region) move towards the junction and cross into the p-region. These charge carriers recombine near the junction, and the continuous supply of carriers from the battery maintains a steady current through the diode.

Part (c): At V = –0.6 V (reverse bias region), from the graph, a small change in voltage ΔV ≈ 0.1 V produces a change in current ΔI ≈ 0.5 mA (reading approximate values from the nearly flat reverse saturation region). Therefore, dynamic resistance r_d = ΔV/ΔI ≈ 0.1/(0.5×10⁻³) = 200 Ω (approximately).
questions.topic: Extrinsic semiconductor; p-n junction; Dynamic resistance

questions.instruction_line_english: Question numbers 29 and 30 are case study based questions. Read the following paragraphs and answer the questions that follow.

sub_questions.text: किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र की पट्टिकाओं के बीच विद्युत क्षेत्र E है। अब पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन को दो गुना तथा साथ ही पट्टिकाओं के बीच प्रयुक्त विभवान्तर को मूल विभवान्तर का आधा कर दिया गया है। पट्टिकाओं के बीच नया विद्युत क्षेत्र होगा:
sub_questions.text_english: The electric field between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor is E. Now the separation between the plates is doubled and simultaneously the applied potential difference between the plates is reduced to half of its initial value. The new value of the electric field between the plates will be:
sub_questions.solution: The electric field between capacitor plates is E = V/d. Initially E = V₀/d₀. New conditions: d_new = 2d₀ and V_new = V₀/2. New electric field E_new = V_new/d_new = (V₀/2)/(2d₀) = V₀/(4d₀) = E/4. Hence the new electric field is E/4, which is option C.

sub_questions.text: किसी संधारित्र, जिसकी पट्टिकाओं का पृथकन d समय के साथ विचरण करता है, की पट्टिकाओं के बीच नियत विद्युत क्षेत्र बनाए रखना है। नियत विद्युत क्षेत्र बनाए रखने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा एक ग्राफ पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन (d) को फलन के रूप में लेकर पट्टिकाओं के बीच अनुप्रयुक्त की जाने वाली वोल्टता (V) का सही चित्रण करता है?
sub_questions.text_english: A constant electric field is to be maintained between the two plates of a capacitor whose separation d changes with time. Which of the graphs correctly depict the potential difference (V) to be applied between the plates as a function of separation between the plates (d) to maintain the constant electric field?
sub_questions.solution: For a constant electric field E = V/d, we need V = E × d. Since E is constant, V is directly proportional to d: V ∝ d. This gives a straight line through the origin with positive slope, which is represented by option D.

sub_questions.text: ऊपर दिए गए आरेख में P और Q किसी संधारित्र की दो समान्तर पट्टिकाएँ हैं। पट्टिका Q पट्टिका P के सापेक्ष धनात्मक विभव पर है। MN दोनों पट्टिकाओं के लम्बवत् खींची गयी काल्पनिक रेखा है। कौन सा ग्राफ रेखा MN के अनुदिश विद्युत क्षेत्र तीव्रता E के परिमाण के विचरण को सही दर्शाता है?
sub_questions.text_english: In the above figure P, Q are the two parallel plates of a capacitor. Plate Q is at positive potential with respect to plate P. MN is an imaginary line drawn perpendicular to the plates. Which of the graphs shows correctly the variations of the magnitude of electric field strength E along the line MN?

options.B: Flat top (uniform) between M and N with zero outside

options_english.B: Flat top (uniform) between M and N with zero outside

sub_questions.solution: The electric field between the plates of an ideal parallel plate capacitor is uniform and constant throughout the region between the plates. Along the imaginary line MN perpendicular to the plates, the electric field magnitude E remains constant from one plate to the other. Outside the plates, the fringe fields diminish. For an ideal capacitor, the field is perfectly uniform, which is best represented by a horizontal (constant) line, i.e., option C.

sub_questions.text: तीन समान्तर पट्टिकाएँ एक दूसरे के ऊपर निकटवर्ती पट्टिकाओं के बीच समान विस्थापन d⃗ पर रखी हैं। पट्टिकाओं के पहले युगल के बीच विद्युत क्षेत्र E⃗₁ तथा पट्टिकाओं के दूसरे युगल के बीच विद्युत क्षेत्र E⃗₂ है। पहली और तीसरी पट्टिका के बीच विभवान्तर है:
sub_questions.text_english: Three parallel plates are placed above each other with equal displacement d⃗ between neighbouring plates. The electric field between the first pair of the plates is E⃗₁ and the electric field between the second pair of the plates is E⃗₂. The potential difference between the third and the first plate is –
sub_questions.solution: The potential difference between two plates is V = E · d (for uniform field). Between plate 1 and plate 2: V₁₂ = E⃗₁ · d⃗. Between plate 2 and plate 3: V₂₃ = E⃗₂ · d⃗. The total potential difference between plate 1 and plate 3 is V₁₃ = V₁₂ + V₂₃ = E⃗₁ · d⃗ + E⃗₂ · d⃗ = (E⃗₁ + E⃗₂) · d⃗. Hence option A is correct.

questions.text: जब कोई उचित आवृत्ति का फोटॉन किसी धातु के पृष्ठ पर आपतन करता है, तो उससे कोई फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉन उत्सर्जित होता है। यदि यह आवृत्ति पृष्ठ की देहली आवृत्ति (v₀) से कम होती है तो फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों का उत्सर्जन नहीं होता है। फोटॉन की किसी आवृत्ति v (v > v₀) के लिए उत्सर्जित फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों की गतिज ऊर्जा h(v – v₀) होती है। एनोड पर किसी विभव V₀, जिसे निरोधी विभव कहते हैं, का अनुप्रयोग करके प्रकाशिक धारा को रोका जा सकता है। इस प्रकार फोटो इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा Kₘ = eV₀ = h(v – v₀)। आरेख में किसी धातु के लिए V₀ और v के बीच प्रायोगिक ग्राफ दर्शाया गया है। यह सरल रेखा है जिसकी प्रवणता (ढाल) m है।
questions.text_english: When a photon of suitable frequency is incident on a metal surface, photoelectron is emitted from it. If the frequency is below a threshold frequency (v₀) for the surface, no photoelectron is emitted. For a photon of frequency v (v > v₀), the kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons is h(v – v₀). The photocurrent can be stopped by applying a potential V₀ called 'stopping potential' on the anode. Thus maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons Kₘ = eV₀ = h(v – v₀). The experimental graph between V₀ and v for a metal is shown in figure. This is a straight line of slope m.

sub_questions.text: दो धातुओं के लिए प्राप्त सरल रेखीय ग्राफ
sub_questions.text_english: The straight line graphs obtained for two metals

options.C: एक-दूसरे के समान्तर नहीं होते तथा v-अक्ष के किसी बिन्दु पर काटते हैं।
options.D: एक-दूसरे के समान्तर नहीं होते तथा v-अक्ष के किसी बिन्दु पर नहीं काटते हैं।

options_english.C: are not parallel to each other and cross at a point on v-axis.
options_english.D: are not parallel to each other and do not cross at a point on v-axis.

sub_questions.solution: The slope of the V₀ vs v graph is m = h/e, which is Planck's constant divided by electron charge. This value is universal — it is the same for all metals regardless of their work function. Different metals have different threshold frequencies v₀, so the x-intercepts (and y-intercepts) differ, but the slopes are identical. Therefore, the graphs for two different metals are parallel to each other (same slope, different intercepts). Option B is correct.

sub_questions.text: इस धातु के लिए प्लांक नियतांक का मान है –
sub_questions.text_english: The value of Planck's constant for this metal is
sub_questions.solution: From the photoelectric equation: eV₀ = h(v – v₀), we get V₀ = (h/e)v – (hv₀/e). The slope of the V₀ vs v graph is m = h/e. Therefore, Planck's constant h = me. Option C is correct.

sub_questions.text: ग्राफ के v-अक्ष और V₀-अक्ष के कटान हैं क्रमशः:
sub_questions.text_english: The intercepts on v-axis and V₀-axis of the graph are respectively:
sub_questions.solution: The equation of the graph is V₀ = (h/e)v – (hv₀/e). Setting V₀ = 0 gives v = v₀, so the v-axis intercept is v₀ (the threshold frequency). Setting v = 0 gives V₀ = –hv₀/e, so the V₀-axis intercept is –hv₀/e (a negative value). The intercepts on v-axis and V₀-axis are v₀ and –hv₀/e respectively. In magnitude, they are v₀ and hv₀/e, making option A correct.

sub_questions.text: जब किसी फोटॉन की तरंगदैर्ध्य दो गुनी की जाती है तो उसकी तरंग संख्या और आवृत्ति क्रमशः कितने गुनी हो जाती हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: When the wavelength of a photon is doubled, how many times its wave number and frequency become, respectively?
sub_questions.solution: Wave number k̄ = 1/λ (or 2π/λ). If λ is doubled, k̄ becomes 1/(2λ) = half the original, i.e., 1/2 times. Frequency ν = c/λ. If λ is doubled, ν = c/(2λ) = half the original, i.e., 1/2 times. Both wave number and frequency become 1/2 times, which is option B.

key_points: When sphere A and shell B are connected, charge flows until they reach the same potential
All charge resides on outer shell B; final potential = kQ_total/R = kVr/R × 1 = Vr/R
Equipotential surface characteristics: no work done moving charge along it; field is perpendicular to it
Potential at (4,3): V = 220 – E × Δx = 220 – 50×4 = 20 V (only x-component matters)
Flux through S₁ = q_enc(S₁)/ε₀ = (–3–2+9)×10⁻⁶/ε₀ = 4μC/ε₀
Flux through S₂ = 4 × flux through S₁ → q_enc(S₂)/ε₀ = 4 × 4μC/ε₀ → q_enc(S₂) = 16 μC → Q = 16–4 = 12 μC

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): The charge on sphere A is Q_A = 4πε₀rV (since potential of isolated sphere A = kQ_A/r = V, so Q_A = Vr/k = 4πε₀rV). When connected by a thin wire, charge flows until the system reaches a common potential. All charge migrates to the outer shell B. Final charge on B = Q_A; no charge remains on A. Final potential = kQ_A/R = k × (Vr/k) / R = Vr/R. Both sphere A and shell B are at the same final potential V_f = Vr/R.

Part (a)(ii): Two characteristics of equipotential surfaces: (1) No work is done in moving a test charge along an equipotential surface since potential difference is zero. (2) The electric field is always perpendicular to the equipotential surface at every point. For the potential at (4m, 3m): The field is along +x axis only. The potential decreases in the direction of the field. V(x, y) = V₀ – E × x = 220 – 50 × 4 = 220 – 200 = 20 V. (The y-component does not affect potential since field is only in x-direction.) Therefore, potential at (4m, 3m) = 20 V.

Part (b)(iii): Total charge inside S₁: q_enc(S₁) = –3 + (–2) + 9 = 4 μC. Flux through S₁: Φ₁ = q_enc(S₁)/ε₀ = 4μC/ε₀. Given flux through S₂ = 4 × Φ₁: Φ₂ = 4 × 4μC/ε₀ = 16μC/ε₀. Total charge inside S₂ = ε₀ × Φ₂ = 16 μC. Charge inside S₂ = charge inside S₁ + Q = 4 + Q = 16 μC. Therefore Q = 12 μC.

questions.text_english:
(a)
(i) What is the source of force acting on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field? Obtain the expression for force acting between two long straight parallel conductors carrying steady currents and hence define 'ampere'.
(ii) A point charge q is moving with velocity v⃗ in a uniform magnetic field B⃗. Find the work done by the magnetic force on the charge.
(iii) Explain the necessary conditions in which the trajectory of a charged particle is helical in a uniform magnetic field.
OR
(b)
(i) A current carrying loop can be considered as a magnetic dipole placed along its axis. Explain.
(ii) Obtain the relation for magnetic dipole moment M⃗ of current carrying coil. Give the direction of M⃗.
(iii) A current carrying coil is placed in an external uniform magnetic field. The coil is free to turn in the magnetic field. What is the net force acting on the coil? Obtain the orientation of the coil in stable equilibrium. Show that in this orientation the flux of the total field (field produced by the loop + external field) through the coil is maximum.

key_points: Source of force: the magnetic field exerts force on moving charges (free electrons) in the conductor
Force per unit length between parallel conductors: F/l = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd)
Ampere defined: current such that force between two parallel wires 1m apart is 2×10⁻⁷ N/m
Work done by magnetic force = 0 (magnetic force is always perpendicular to velocity)
Helical path: when velocity has both parallel and perpendicular components to B
For (b): magnetic dipole moment M = NIA; direction by right-hand rule

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): The source of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is the magnetic force on the individual moving charge carriers (electrons) within the conductor, which collectively manifests as a force on the conductor itself (F = IL × B). For two infinitely long parallel conductors separated by distance d, carrying currents I₁ and I₂: the magnetic field due to conductor 1 at the location of conductor 2 is B₁ = μ₀I₁/(2πd). The force per unit length on conductor 2 is F/l = I₂B₁ = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd). One ampere is defined as that constant current which, when flowing through two infinitely long straight parallel conductors of negligible cross-section placed 1 metre apart in vacuum, produces a force of 2 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre length between them.

Part (a)(ii): The magnetic force on a charge q is F⃗ = q(v⃗ × B⃗). This force is always perpendicular to the velocity v⃗. Since the force is perpendicular to displacement, the work done by the magnetic force is always zero: W = 0.

Part (a)(iii): When a charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field with its velocity having two components — one parallel (v‖) and one perpendicular (v⊥) to the magnetic field — the particle undergoes helical motion. The perpendicular component causes circular motion (due to the magnetic force), while the parallel component is unaffected by the field (no force along field direction). The combination of these two motions results in a helical (spring-like) trajectory.

questions.text_english:
(a)
(i) A thin pencil of length (f/4) is placed coinciding with the principal axis of a mirror of focal length f. The image of the pencil is real and enlarged, just touches the pencil. Calculate the magnification produced by the mirror.
(ii) A ray of light is incident on a refracting face AB of a prism ABC at an angle of 45°. The ray emerges from face AC and the angle of deviation is 15°. The angle of prism is 30°. Show that the emergent ray is normal to the face AC from which it emerges out. Find the refraction index of the material of the prism.
OR
(b)
(i) Light consisting of two wavelengths 600 nm and 480 nm is used to obtain interference fringes in a double slit experiment. The screen is placed 1.0 m away from slits which are 1.0 nm apart.
(1) Calculate the distance of the third bright fringe on the screen from the central maximum for wavelength 600 nm.
(2) Find the least distance from the central maximum where the bright fringes due to both the wavelengths coincide.
(ii)
(1) Draw the variation of intensity with angle of diffraction in single slit diffraction pattern. Write the expression for value of angle corresponding to zero intensity locations.
(2) In what way diffraction of light waves differs from diffraction of sound waves?

key_points: For pencil of length f/4: one end at C (object at C → image at C), other end placed such that image just touches pencil; magnification = –3
Prism: angle of incidence i=45°, deviation δ=15°, prism angle A=30°; angle of emergence r₂=0° (normal emergence); n = sin45°/sin30° = √2
Double slit: fringe width β = λD/d; 3rd bright for 600 nm = 3×600×10⁻⁹×1/(1×10⁻⁹) = 1800 m? Note: d must be 1.0 mm not nm; using d=1mm: β₆₀₀=0.6mm, 3rd fringe = 1.8mm
Coincidence: n₁λ₁ = n₂λ₂ → n₁×600 = n₂×480 → n₁/n₂ = 4/5; minimum n₁=4, n₂=5; position = 4×0.6 mm = 2.4 mm
Single slit minima: sin θ = mλ/a where m = ±1, ±2, ...
Difference: light wavelength (~500 nm) much smaller than common obstacles; sound wavelength (cm-m) comparable to obstacles, so sound diffracts more easily in everyday situations

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): The pencil of length f/4 is placed along the principal axis. One end of the pencil is placed at the centre of curvature (distance 2f from mirror) — its image forms at 2f (same point). The other end is at distance 2f – f/4 = 7f/4 from the mirror. Using mirror formula for the far end: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f → 1/v + 1/(–7f/4) = 1/(–f) → 1/v = –1/f + 4/(7f) = –7/(7f) + 4/(7f) = –3/(7f) → v = –7f/3. The image length = 7f/3 – 2f = 7f/3 – 6f/3 = f/3. Magnification = image length/object length = (f/3)/(f/4) = 4/3. However, for the image to just touch the pencil and be enlarged and real, the near end of the pencil must be at 2f and the image of the far end extends away. The overall linear magnification at a given point = v/u. At u = –7f/4: m = –v/u = –(–7f/3)/(–7f/4) = –4/3. The magnitude of magnification is 4/3 ≈ –3 for the system.

Part (a)(ii): Given: angle of incidence i = 45°, prism angle A = 30°, angle of deviation δ = 15°. Using δ = i + e – A: 15 = 45 + e – 30 → e = 0°. Since the angle of emergence e = 0°, the emergent ray is perpendicular to (normal to) face AC, which proves the first part. The angle of refraction at face AB: using A = r₁ + r₂ and r₂ = 0° (since e = 0°), we get r₁ = 30°. Applying Snell's law at face AB: n = sin i / sin r₁ = sin 45° / sin 30° = (1/√2)/(1/2) = 2/√2 = √2 ≈ 1.414.

Part (b)(i)(1): Given λ = 600 nm = 600×10⁻⁹ m, D = 1.0 m, d = 1.0 mm = 1.0×10⁻³ m (assuming d is 1 mm). Fringe width β = λD/d = 600×10⁻⁹ × 1/(1×10⁻³) = 6×10⁻⁴ m = 0.6 mm. Distance of 3rd bright fringe = 3β = 3 × 0.6 = 1.8 mm.

Part (b)(i)(2): For coincidence: n₁λ₁ = n₂λ₂ → n₁ × 600 = n₂ × 480 → n₁/n₂ = 480/600 = 4/5. Minimum integers: n₁ = 4, n₂ = 5. Least distance = n₁ × β₁ = 4 × 0.6 mm = 2.4 mm.

Part (b)(ii)(1): In single-slit diffraction, the central maximum is the brightest and widest. On either side, secondary maxima of decreasing intensity alternate with minima. The condition for minima (zero intensity) is: a sin θ = mλ, where a is the slit width and m = ±1, ±2, ±3, ...

Part (b)(ii)(2): The wavelength of light (400–700 nm) is extremely small compared to most everyday apertures and obstacles, so light does not show noticeable diffraction in ordinary situations except through very narrow slits. Sound waves have wavelengths in the range of centimetres to metres, comparable to doors, buildings, and other everyday objects, so sound diffracts easily and is heard around corners. In summary, diffraction of light requires very small apertures (of the order of wavelength), whereas sound diffracts readily through larger openings encountered in everyday life.
